IRON SHEETS LOAN PROJECT The Iron Sheets Loan Project is designed to support workers in improving their housing conditions by providing affordable loans to purchase iron sheets (roofing materials). Through this initiative workers will access quality roofing materials and repay the cost in manageable installments over an agreed period. The project aims to promote safe durable and decent housing while reducing the financial burden of making large upfront payments. It also contributes to workers’ welfare dignity and long-term socio-economic stability. Many workers live in inadequate housing due to low incomes making it difficult to afford durable roofing materials. As a result they face poor living conditions health risks and limited access to financing for home improvements compounded by low savings capacity.

IEF PROJECT LOAN IEF is a project that provided solar loans to workers, but many workers are unable to repay these loans within a short period. We have therefore introduced a recovery project in which we pay the full loan amount at once, and the worker repays us back in manageable installments. The initial problem addressed by this project is that many borrowers are unable to repay their existing loans on time due to financial constraints, leading to accumulating debt and financial stress. To resolve this, the project proposes paying off the full loan amount on behalf of the borrowers, allowing them to repay in smaller, manageable installments

BUYING STOVES LOANS This investment project aims to provide affordable loans to workers to enable them to purchase improved cooking stoves. These stoves are energy-efficient cost-effective and environmentally friendly compared to traditional cooking methods.The loan scheme will enable workers to acquire the stoves through affordable manageable installments paid over an agreed period. The initiative seeks to improve workers’ living conditions while promoting sustainable energy use and reducing household expenses related to cooking fuel Before the implementation of this project many workers face several challenges including: High expenditure on cooking fuel such as firewood and charcoal Use of inefficient traditional stoves that consume more fuel Exposure to smoke leading to health issues such as respiratory problems Limited access to upfront capital to purchase improved stoves Environmental degradation due to excessive use of firewood

TEA PLANTATION MAINTENANCE This project focuses on improving the productivity and sustainability of tea plantations through proper field maintenance practices and the application of organic manure. The investment includes activities such as plucking weeding soil conservation and the use of organic fertilizers (such as buying animal manure) to restore soil fertility. The project aims to enhance tea quality and yield while reducing dependence on chemical fertilizers and promoting environmentally friendly farming practices The key challenges include declining soil fertility from continuous tea cultivation leading to reduced yields and lower green leaf quality. Farmers also face high fertilizer costs and limited access to inputs along with poor plantation management practices such as delayed pruning and inadequate weeding. In addition soil erosion limited knowledge of organic manure use and climate variability further negatively affect tea productivity.

metadata.name: ENVIRONMENT: INSTALLATION OF SOLAR PANELS AND ELECTRICAL APPLIANCES

text: ENVIRONMENT: INSTALLATION OF SOLAR PANELS AND ELECTRICAL APPLIANCES The project is an initiative that stems from the need identified in the needs assessment carried out by our committee in 2025, the idea is to install solar panels for the generation of electrical energy in homes that are owned by workers, helping to avoid environmental wear and tear by generating clean and renewable energy and providing appliances such as pots, heaters, air fryers, induction stoves, and others to gradually migrate to electrical energy from solar panels and eliminate the use of gas or wood burning appliances, thereby reducing the carbon footprint generated by all workers' homes within the scope of the certificate. The project will be funded 100% with the premium received by our committee. The results of the needs assessment showed that our workers and their families cook using mainly LP gas and this represents an expense that seriously impacts their economy when, without warning, they run out of gas to continue cooking and have to buy it overnight. In addition, as a second source of energy for cooking, many families use firewood, which when burned pollutes the atmosphere and increases the risk of families suffering respiratory diseases when they inhale the smoke that is generated. That is why there is a need for workers' homes to migrate and start using clean and renewable energies that do not cause pollution, seeking to make homes self-sustainable first by generating their own electricity and then equipping them with devices that work based on this electricity to meet the most basic needs such as electricity, hot water, cooking, etc.
